title: Protocol for Studying Reprogramming of Mouse Pancreatic Acinar Cells to β-like Cells
author: Elhanani, Walker
materials: This stage allows the isolation of pancreatic exocrine cell clusters and their infection with adenoviral vectors to induce their reprogramming to insulin- or somatostatin-expressing cells. As we wish to study the formation of newly formed insulin-positive cells, this protocol includes a stage for elimination of native β cells by treatment with the β cell toxin alloxan. This protocol can be used for applications other than studies of β cell reprogramming. In this case, alloxan treatment is not required as native β cells comprise a small fraction of pancreatic cells and will not interfere with most other applications.1.Sacrifice the desired number of mice (8–12 week old) by cervical dislocation (in accordance with local IACUC guidelines).2.Place on ice a 6-well plate containing 4 mL of cold HBSS wash solution per well.3.Dissect the mouse and excise the pancreas into a single well.4.Wash the tissue in the well and transfer to a new well containing cold HBSS wash solution.5.Repeat steps 3–4 for the desired number of mice. Do not let tissues stand on ice for longer than 30 min.6.Transfer one pancreas into 60 mm tissue culture plate containing 5 mL of cold collagenase solution. Mince the tissue with scissors (Figure 1B) and gently transfer to a 50 mL conical tube using 1 mL pipettor trimmed at the end (to reduce shear forces on the cells, Figure 1C). Place the conical tube in ice while processing the remaining pancreata.7.Incubate for 12 min at 37°C. After the first 4 min of incubation, and every 2 min until the end of the incubation: pipette the tissues gently five times up and down using 1 mL trimmed pipette.CRITICAL: Collagenase digestion is a critical stage as over-digestion of the tissue can impair cell viability (Figure 1D) and reprogramming efficiency. Batch to batch variation in collagenase may affect its activity and the time of digestion may require calibration to optimize viability at the end of the protocol.8.To each tube (one digested pancreas in each tube), add 45 mL of ice cold HBSS wash solution.9.Perform two washes by centrifugation of the cells at 200 × g for 3 min followed by aspiration of the supernatant and adding an additional 45 mL of HBSS wash solution. After the first wash, the desired number of pancreata can be combined in a single 50 mL conical tube.10.Gently resuspend the pellet in 5 mL HBSS wash solution using 1 mL trimmed pipette and then add HBSS wash solution to a total volume of 30 mL.11.To obtain desirable size of cell clusters and to remove clumps of undigested tissue, filter through a standard metal tea strainer followed by filtration through a 100 μm cell strainer.12.Centrifuge at 200 × g for 3 min and aspirate the supernatant leaving ∼3 mL of liquid.13.Alloxan treatment (Figures 1F and 1G):a.Prepare 1M stock solution in DDW.CRITICAL: alloxan is unstable in solution, alloxan stock solution must be prepared fresh immediately before use.b.Dilute alloxan stock solution 1:100 (10 mM) in desired volume of HBSS wash solution.c.For each pancreas: prepare 3 × 15 mL conical tubes each containing 9 mL of HBSS+alloxan (Figure 1E, left panel).d.Resuspend the cell pellet in 3 mL HBSS wash solution and transfer gently 1 mL to each of the 15 mL conical tubes containing the alloxan solution.e.Incubate for 10 min at room temperature (20°–30°C) and allow cell clusters to sediment by gravity (Figure 1E, right panel). This helps to deplete dead cells and enrich for large cell clusters.Optional: alloxan treatment depletes native β cells from the culture. This step is critical when studying reprogramming of exocrine to endocrine cells. However, as native β cells comprise a small fraction of the cells in the culture, their presence will not interfere with most other application of this protocol. Hence, if this protocol is to be used for other application than reprogramming, use HBSS wash solution without alloxan in this step.14.Aspirate alloxan solution leaving ∼1 mL at the bottom of the tube. Resuspend the cell pellet with trimmed 1 mL pipette tip and from each tube transfer to a new 15 mL tube containing 9 mL of HBSS wash solution (3 tubes per pancreas, Figure 1E, left panel). Allow cell clusters to sediment by gravity to the bottom of the tube for 7 min.15.Repeat the last step but this time combine three tubes containing cells from the same pancreas into one 15 mL tube.16.From this stage, all subsequent steps should be performed in the tissue culture hood. Aspirate the HBSS wash solution from the 15 mL conical tube leaving a minimal volume at the bottom.17.Resuspend the cells gently using a trimmed 1 mL pipette tip and resuspend in 3 mL of Waymouth’s culture medium in a 50 mL conical tube.18.Plating of cells: for reproducibility, in every experiment the ratio of virus titer to the number of cells should remain constant. Since cells are clustered, it is impractical to count them. As an alternative protein content is measured and 850 μg protein from cells is plated per well in a 6-well plate:a.Mix cells gently by swirling the conical tube and immediately transfer 100 μL of cells to an Eppendorf tube.b.Wash the cells twice with PBS by centrifugation of the cells at 500 × g for 4 min.c.Lyse the cells using 100 μL of lysis buffer.d.Measure protein concentration using Bio-Rad protein assay.e.Calculate the protein concentration in the original tube containing cells.f.Dilute the cells to a final concentration of 1,700 μg protein equivalent /mL with Waymouth’s medium.g.Add 1.5 mL of Waymouth’s medium to the desired amount of wells in 6-well plates (non-collagen coated at this stage).h.To each well add 0.5 mL of cell suspension.CRITICAL: exocrine cell clusters sink very fast. While plating, it is important to continually and gently swirl the tube containing the cells in order to uniformly mix them. Otherwise, a non- uniform number of clusters will be plated in each well.19.Transfer the plates to a standard tissue culture incubator (37°C, 5% CO2) while preparing the adenoviruses for infection.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and vectors
steps.instruction: Amplify, aliquot, and determine the titer of all adenoviral vectors to be used. Prepare fresh HBSS wash solution and collagenase P solution, keep both on ice. Prepare collagen‑coated plates (see next step) in advance.

steps.title: Coat plates with collagen
steps.instruction: Dilute Type I collagen 1:10 in double‑distilled water. Add the diluted collagen to each well of the chosen tissue‑culture plates, seal with parafilm and incubate 16–20 h at 4 °C. Aspirate the collagen solution, wash wells twice with PBS, and let plates dry in the hood for 2–20 h. Use plates immediately or seal and store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Euthanize mice and collect pancreas
steps.instruction: Sacrifice 8–12‑week‑old mice by cervical dislocation (IACUC approved). Place a 6‑well plate on ice containing 4 mL cold HBSS wash solution per well. Dissect each mouse, excise the pancreas into a well, wash the tissue, and transfer to a new well with cold HBSS. Repeat for all mice, keeping tissues on ice ≤30 min.

steps.title: Wash and mince pancreas in collagenase
steps.instruction: Transfer one pancreas into a 60‑mm culture plate containing 5 mL cold collagenase solution. Mince with scissors, then gently transfer the minced tissue to a 50‑mL conical tube using a 1‑mL pipette tip trimmed at the end. Keep the tube on ice while processing remaining pancreata.

steps.title: Digest tissue with collagenase
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 37 °C for 12 min. After the first 4 min, and then every 2 min, gently pipette the tissue up and down five times with the trimmed 1‑mL pipette. Over‑digestion reduces viability; adjust time if needed.

steps.title: Quench digestion and wash cells
steps.instruction: Add 45 mL ice‑cold HBSS wash solution to each tube. Perform two washes: centrifuge at 200 × g for 3 min, aspirate supernatant, and add another 45 mL HBSS. After the first wash, combine pancreata from multiple mice if desired.

steps.title: Adjust volume and filter cell suspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL HBSS wash solution, then bring the total volume to 30 mL with HBSS. Filter sequentially through a standard metal tea strainer and then a 100 µm cell strainer to remove undigested clumps.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect cell clusters
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtered suspension at 200 × g for 3 min, then aspirate supernatant leaving approximately 3 mL liquid.

steps.title: Alloxan treatment to deplete β cells
steps.instruction: Prepare a fresh 1 M alloxan stock in DDW and dilute 1:100 with HBSS to obtain 10 mM alloxan. For each pancreas, set up three 15‑mL conical tubes each containing 9 mL HBSS + alloxan. Resuspend the cell pellet in 3 mL HBSS, transfer 1 mL to each tube, and incubate 10 min at room temperature (20–30 °C). Allow clusters to settle by gravity.

steps.title: Remove alloxan and resuspend cells
steps.instruction: Aspirate the alloxan solution leaving ~1 mL, resuspend the pellet, and transfer to a new 15‑mL tube containing 9 mL HBSS (repeat for the three tubes). Let clusters settle 7 min, then combine the three tubes into one 15‑mL tube and let settle again. Aspirate HBSS leaving a minimal volume.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in Waymouth’s medium
steps.instruction: Gently resuspend the cell pellet in 3 mL Waymouth’s culture medium in a 50‑mL conical tube.

steps.title: Measure protein and plate cells
steps.instruction: For reproducible virus‑to‑cell ratios, plate 850 µg protein per well of a 6‑well plate (non‑collagen‑coated at this stage).

substeps.instruction: Swirl the cell suspension, transfer 100 µL to an Eppendorf tube.
Wash cells twice with PBS (centrifuge 500 × g, 4 min each).
Lyse cells with 100 µL lysis buffer.
Determine protein concentration using a Bio‑Rad protein assay.
Calculate the concentration in the original tube and dilute to 1 700 µg protein / mL with Waymouth’s medium.
Add 1.5 mL Waymouth’s medium to each well, then add 0.5 mL of the cell suspension.
Continuously swirl the cell tube while plating to keep clusters uniformly suspended.

steps.title: Incubate plates and prepare adenoviruses
steps.instruction: Place the seeded plates in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator. While the cells attach, prepare the adenoviral vectors for infection (PDX1, NGN3, MafA) at the calibrated titers.

steps.title: Change culture medium every two days
steps.instruction: Replace the medium on day 2 and every 2 days thereafter. Cells begin attaching to the collagen‑coated plates after ~48 h and form a monolayer by day 6.

steps.title: Harvest RNA for gene expression analysis
steps.instruction: At the desired time point (e.g., 3 days post‑isolation), aspirate culture medium, add Tri‑reagent to lyse cells, isolate RNA, synthesize cDNA using standard protocols, and perform qRT‑PCR for endocrine genes. Verify RNA integrity (gel or TapeStation) especially if earlier time points are used.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate culture medium and wash cells once with PBS.
Treat with 0.025 % trypsin (1:2 diluted in PBS) for 12 min at 37 °C.
Pipette up/down 10–15 times to dissociate clusters.
Quench trypsin with 100 µL FBS in the same tube.
Centrifuge 5 min at 500 × g, wash twice with FACS buffer (PBS, 2 mM EDTA, 2.5 % FBS).
Centrifuge again 5 min at 500 × g, aspirate buffer.
Resuspend pellet in fixable viability dye eFluor450 (1:1 000 in FACS buffer).
Incubate 30 min on ice, wash once (500 × g, 5 min) and resuspend in FACS buffer.

steps.title: Sort live cells for RNA extraction
steps.instruction: If gene‑expression analysis of sorted populations is required:

substeps.instruction: Pass the cell suspension through a 35 µm cell strainer.
Gate live cells (eFluor450‑negative) on the flow cytometer.
Sort desired populations directly into lysis buffer containing an RNA‑extraction kit (e.g., RNeasy Micro).
Extract RNA and proceed with cDNA synthesis and qPCR or RNA‑seq.

steps.title: Intracellular hormone staining for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: If hormone production analysis is required:

substeps.instruction: Fix cells in 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS for 10 min.
Centrifuge 600 × g for 5 min and resuspend pellet in PBST.
Perform intracellular immunostaining using the protocol described earlier (including 600 × g, 5 min washes between steps).
Pass the stained suspension through a 35 µm cell strainer.
Analyze on the flow cytometer, gating live cells based on eFluor450.
